answer: Orange dotted underlines mark terms that Spideryarn’s **Glossary** has defined for the article. Point at a term to see its definition; on a touchscreen, tap it. These underlines remain visible in every mode once the glossary exists. See [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary).

Every article starts private. On its Metadata page, open **Access & sharing** and choose one:

- **Create a link** makes a private link for anyone you send it to. They can read without an account, but the article is not listed publicly and they cannot add notes or start AI work.
- **Share with anyone…** makes it public. It appears on the public shelf, so anyone can find and read it; visitors still cannot add notes or start AI work.

Before either option takes effect, Spideryarn shows what the colleague will receive and asks you to confirm that you have the right to share the text. See [Sharing an article, and the public shelf](/help/sharing).

**Skim** gives you a guided route through an article using the article’s own sentences, rather than replacing it with a summary. It is useful when you want to see a paper’s shape quickly while still reading passages in context. ([Skim](/help/mode-skim))

It offers three depths:

- **Gist**: a handful of stops
- **More**: about a dozen stops
- **Most**: a larger share of the article

Each stop has a cue explaining what to look for. Use **‹** and **›**, or **←** and **→**, to move between stops. The route is planned around what you said you want from the article, and deeper passes may include earlier stops.

No. Your allowance counts articles you **add**, not modes you open. Generating modes, chatting, asking questions and re-running modes are included; switching an article to **High-powered AI** is the only other action that counts. See [Plans](/help/plans).

The first time you open **Summary**, the AI writes it; this can take seconds or a minute or more. Keep a Spideryarn tab open while it works, because closing every tab pauses the job. If it remains stuck, try **Retry**; for a stage that failed during article import, **Retry** skips stages that already worked. See [Waiting for a mode](/help/waiting-and-cost) and [Adding an article](/help/adding-articles).

If it still does not appear, the Help pages do not specify a further Summary-specific fix. Send **Feedback** from the page where it is stuck, describing what you expected and what you saw; you can include extra diagnostics. See [Telling us something](/help/feedback).

The box with orange top and bottom edges on the left is the **screen marker** on the spine. It shows which part of the article is currently visible; its height shows how much of the article fits on your screen. It moves as you scroll. See [Reading the spine](/help/spine).

Yes. On an article’s **Metadata** page, press **Export this article**. It downloads a zip containing everything Spideryarn holds for that article, including your comments, bookmarks, highlights and chats, as plain files you can open without Spideryarn. The original web page or PDF and its images are not included. See [Your data: export, archive, delete](/help/your-data).

Yes. Spideryarn works on phones and tablets, including iPads, though it works best on a large screen. On a narrow screen:

- A mode panel covers the article; press **Plain** to return to the text.
- Tap the spine twice: the first tap shows a section card, and the second goes there.
- Tap a paragraph to show its margin controls.
- Press and hold to select words, highlight them, or add a comment.
- If Spideryarn is on your home screen, use the **↩ back to …** button because there may be no browser Back button.

See [Phones and tablets](/help/touch).

**Summary** reformule l’article en quelques paragraphes, en version **Brief** ou **Fuller**, ou sous forme de **Thread**. Chaque partie renvoie aux passages sur lesquels elle s’appuie, mais elle laisse de côté une grande partie du raisonnement : utilisez-la comme une carte, pas comme un remplacement de l’article ([Summary](/help/mode-summary)).

**Skim** vous fait parcourir une sélection de phrases de l’auteur, dans leur contexte et à leur emplacement dans l’article. Il organise ces passages en parcours de profondeur croissante : **Gist**, **More** ou **Most**, avec une courte indication de ce qu’il faut regarder ([Skim](/help/mode-skim)).

En bref : choisissez **Summary** pour comprendre rapidement l’idée générale ; choisissez **Skim** pour parcourir directement les mots de l’auteur sans lire tout l’article d’un coup.

The Help pages do not say whether EPUB files from Kindle are supported. They only say you can add a **PDF** or a web page saved as **HTML** by pressing **File** or dropping the file into **Add an article**. If your EPUB is not accepted, please use **Feedback** to ask the Spideryarn team. [Adding an article](/help/adding-articles)

The Help pages do not say whether Spideryarn offers a student discount. Plans and prices are described on the pricing page, and billing details are under **Plan** on your profile; for a definitive answer, use [Feedback](/help/feedback).

No. The Help pages do not describe real-time collaborative annotation. You can share an article privately or publicly; visitors can read your existing comments and bookmarks, but they cannot add or change their own. See [Sharing an article, and the public shelf](/help/sharing) and [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments).

The Help pages do not describe an API for driving Spideryarn from your own scripts. They only explain using the app through its web interface, command bar, bookmarklet-style URL for adding an article, and sharing links. For a definitive answer, use **Feedback** to ask the people who make Spideryarn ([Feedback](/help/feedback)).
